features.name: argument_hedging_share
features.definition: What proportion of the OP's own assertive sentences in the argument use hedging or qualifying language rather than absolute declarative phrasing?
features.spec: Read only the argument text (OP's body). Consider the OP's own declarative claims/assertions (ignore questions, quotations of others not adopted by the OP, and any view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome). Count claims that use hedging/qualifying language (e.g., 'might', 'perhaps', 'I think', 'in some cases', 'generally', 'tend to', 'seems') as hedged; claims stated flatly or absolutely (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'obviously', unqualified 'X is Y') as absolute. Return hedged / (hedged + absolute) as a number in [0,1]. If argument is missing or malformed return null; if there are no eligible claims return null.

h0: argument_hedging_share has no association with the likelihood of view change.
h1: Higher argument_hedging_share is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
note: Operationalized as a continuous share of hedged vs absolute claims in the OP's argument; the hedged-vs-absolute comparison is a continuum, not two separate groups. Current argument text may include edits or outcome announcements (the prompt excludes them semantically, but edit timing is unknown). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.
